{{Top}} {{Update|[[Reign of the Empire: The Mask of Fear]], [[Star Wars: Doctor Aphra Book VII: Unspeakable Rebel Superweapon]], [[Shadow Fall: An Alphabet Squadron Novel|Shadow Fall]], [[TIE Fighter Owners' Workshop Manual]], [[Star Wars: The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire]], [[Star Wars Bestiary, Vol. 1: Creatures of the Galaxy]]}} {{TitleOrPosition |image=[[File:Emperor_Palpatine_AoN.png]] |name=Galactic Emperor |establishedby=[[Galactic Empire]]{{Film|III}} |dateestablished=[[19 BBY]]''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' |datesuspended=[[4 ABY]] |datereestablished=[[35 ABY]]''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of {{Film|IX}} to [[35 ABY]]. |dateabolished= |government=*Galactic Empire{{Film|IV}} *[[First Order]] {{C|secretly}}''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: Expanded Edition]]'' |organization= |type=[[Emperor|Sovereign ruler]]''[[The Star Wars Book]]'' |term=[[Death|Life]] |powers=[[Dictatorship|Autocratic rule]] |duties=Autocratic monarch of the Galactic Empire }} {{Quote|The Emperor is not as forgiving as I am.|Darth Vader|{{Film|VI}}}} The '''Galactic Emperor''', also referred to as the '''Imperial Emperor''', the '''Imperial king''', the '''Sith Emperor''', or simply the '''Emperor''', was the [[King|sovereign ruler]] of the [[Galactic Empire]] during the [[Imperial Era]] of [[Timeline of galactic history|galactic history]]. Despite the existence of the [[Imperial Senate]], the [[Galactic Senate|last remnant]] of the [[Galactic Republic]] in the [[New Order]], the [[Emperor]] was invested with [[Dictatorship|supreme authority]] over both the Imperial [[Imperial Ruling Council|government]] and the [[Imperial Military]]. As such, the Emperor had free rein to [[Politics|govern]] [[the galaxy]] as he so desired, from replacing [[senator]]s with [[Moff]]s as [[Sector|regional]] [[governor]]s, to [[Dissolution of the Imperial Senate|disbanding the Senate]] altogether. In the aftermath of the [[Clone Wars]], the [[Democracy|democratic]] Republic was [[Proclamation of the New Order|transformed]] into an [[Fascism|authoritarian]] state by [[Supreme Chancellor]] [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]], who appointed himself Galactic Emperor in [[19 BBY]]. Unbeknownst to his subjects, Palpatine was in fact the [[Sith Lord]] [[Darth]] Sidious who conspired to take over the Republic and [[Great Jedi Purge|destroy]] the [[Jedi Order]]. Sidious' reign brought the galaxy under the rule of the [[Sith]], which lasted for a generation until the Emperor was [[Battle of Endor|killed]] in [[4 ABY]]. In the ensuing crisis, the Empire broke into factionalism due to the lack of a clear chain of succession, with individuals such as [[Grand General]] [[Levinous]], [[Admiral]] [[Rolas]], and [[Grand Moff]] [[Plorest]] all making efforts to anoint themselves as the new Imperial Emperor. Ultimately, it was [[Fleet Admiral]] [[Gallius Rax]] and his [[Shadow Council]] that seized power, with Rax becoming [[Counselor to the Empire|Emperor in all but name]], while [[Grand Vizier]] [[Mas Amedda]] was forced to serve as a figurehead for the declining Empire. After Rax's [[Battle of Jakku|demise]], the [[Galactic Civil War]] [[Galactic Concordance|concluded]] with the Empire's [[Imperial Instruments of Surrender|capitulation]] to the [[New Republic]] in [[5 ABY]]. During the [[New Republic Era]], the [[First Order]] and the [[Sith Eternal]] emerged from the [[Unknown Regions]] as offshoots of the Emperor's [[Contingency]]. Despite his own [[death]], Sidious returned to oversee the final stage of his plan to create a [[Sith Empire]] that would rule the galaxy forever. In his weakened state, he had considered [[Supreme Leader]] [[Ben Solo|Kylo Ren]] and the [[Padawan|Jedi apprentice]] [[Rey Skywalker|Rey]] as potential successors, but after discovering their nature as a [[Force dyad|dyad in the Force]], Sidious siphoned the energy of their [[Force-bond]] to regain his full strength as the one true Emperor. Before he could unleash the Sith Eternal's [[fleet]], the [[Final Order]], against the galaxy, Sidious was [[Battle of Exegol|destroyed]] by Rey with the help of all the [[Jedi]] who were one with [[the Force]]. As a result of the [[Resistance]] victory, the people of the galaxy were inspired to [[Uprising against the First Order|rise up]] against the [[First Order military|military junta]]. ==Powers== {{Quote|The Emperor has no power to ''veto'' the Rebirth Act. The bill is passed.''"
"''He is the ''Emperor''. This is the ''Empire''. His power, Senator Mothma, is absolute.''"
"''The power of any government is contingent upon the will of the people.|Senator Mon Mothma and Grand Vizier Mas Amedda argue about Palpatine's power in the early months of the Empire|''[[Reign of the Empire: The Mask of Fear]]''}} [[File:EmperorsArrival-SWBC30.png|thumb|left|300px|The Galactic Emperor was the ruler of the galaxy during the Imperial Era.]] The [[Galaxy|Galactic]] [[Emperor]]{{SWE|characters|yoda|Yoda}} was the self-appointed [[King|sovereign ruler]] of the first [[Galactic Empire]].{{Databank|galactic-empire|Galactic Empire}} Replacing the office of [[Supreme Chancellor]], which had been [[Military Creation Act|empowered]] with wartime powers by the [[Galactic Senate]] during the [[Republic Era|last years]] of the [[Galactic Republic|Old Republic]],{{Film|II}} the Emperor was the [[Dictatorship|ultimate authority]] in [[Politics|political]] and military affairs of state. As a result, the Emperor had the power to unilaterally implement policies that affected the Empire as a whole—from directing the [[Imperial Military]] to subjugate entire [[planet]]s,{{Databank|darth-sidious-biography-gallery|Darth Sidious Biography Gallery}} to ordering for their [[Destruction of Alderaan|destruction]]. To that end the Emperor could delegate power to others, allowing him to rule the Empire through subordinates who served as an extension of his authority. The Emperor's power over [[the galaxy]] remained relatively unchallenged until the [[Declaration of the Rebel Alliance|rise]] of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]],{{Databank|emperor-palpatine-darth-sidious|Emperor Palpatine/Darth Sidious}} an organization that was committed to the restoration of [[democracy]].{{Databank|rebel-alliance|Rebel Alliance}} The Emperor also served as the ''de facto'' leader of the [[Imperial Senate]]. Apart from the authority to entirely [[Dissolution of the Imperial Senate|dissolve]] it—something that in theory would only be done for the duration of an emergency{{StoryCite|story=Verge of Greatness|book=From a Certain Point of View}} but in practice would be permanent—and transfer its administrative responsibilities to a cadre of [[Sector|regional]] [[governor]]s the Emperor alone had the power to pass voted laws into action—which he rarely did.{{RebelsMagCite|9|Senate Perspective}} He could also propose bills and legislation like the [[Public Order Resentencing Directive]] and the [[Imperial Emergency Act]],{{Andor|Announcement}} publicly support or object to laws other Senators had proposed,{{TBB|Truth and Consequences}} as well as veto provisions of Senate-approved motions and bills, preventing them from taking full effect. The Emperor would make impromptu appearances to weigh in important matters. In these cases, all military [[officer]]s present in the [[Galactic Senate Chamber|Senate Chamber]] had to stand in attention while all [[senator]]s at the time recognized by the [[Grand Vizier]] were to cede the floor to him immediately. [[File:EmperorAndSenate-TAC.png|thumb|right|300px|The Emperor of the Galactic Empire possessed absolute power over the Imperial Senate in practice.]] Despite the Emperor's considerable power, he still could not technically enforce any law a significant majority of the Senate had objected to.{{TBB|The Clone Conspiracy}} However, Palpatine's steady work to take power away from the Senate,{{Andor|Nobody's Listening!}} instead investing it in the regional governors,''[[Star Wars Rebels: The Visual Guide]]'' and efforts to rule through fear alone eventually enabled him to sidestep the institution all together, dissolving the Senate once he no longer had use of it. ==History== ===Darth Sidious=== ====Establishment==== {{Quote|People ''want'' this. Our trouble isn't that Palpatine is a dictator or that he has total control of the military. Our trouble is that, by and large—all exceptions aside—the citizens of our nation are willing to believe his lies, ignore his purges, and accept his rule in return for stability. They may not want ''him'', but they don't want war. They want anything ''but'' war, and Palpatine has boxed us in so that war appears to be the only way out.''"
"''If people understood—''"
"''They understand. They understand enough. If they hadn't been willing to trade the Jedi for stability, they wouldn't have accepted the Emperor's lies so easily.|Senators Mon Mothma and Bail Organa|}} [[File:Declaration.png|thumb|left|300px|Darth Sidious, publicly known as Sheev Palpatine, declared himself Emperor of the First Galactic Empire.]] At the conclusion of the [[Clone Wars]] in the [[Standard year|year]] [[19 BBY]], the Galactic Republic which had existed for a [[millennium]] was transformed into the Galactic Empire by [[Proclamation of the New Order|proclamation]] of [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]], the last Supreme Chancellor of the Republic. In secret, Palpatine was [[Darth]] Sidious—the [[Dark Lord of the Sith]] who orchestrated the galaxy-wide civil war between the Republic and [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]], as well as the subsequent [[Great Jedi Purge|purge]] of the [[Jedi Order]]. Without the [[Jedi]] to oppose him, Sidious exercised his control over the Galactic Senate by supplanting a thousand years of democracy with the absolute rule of the [[Sith]] through himself as Galactic Emperor. Having attained ultimate power, the Emperor had no further use in cultivating two identities.{{Databank|palpatine-biography-gallery|Palpatine Biography Gallery}} Although he would rule the galaxy through fear and tyranny as "Emperor Palpatine," he was henceforth Darth Sidious in thought and action. ====Consolidating power==== {{Quote|Since my ascension, I have allowed a convenient fiction to persist—that the Empire is merely a continuation of the Republic. The Imperial Senate remains—an illusion of many voices coming together to govern. In truth, there is only one voice. Mine.|Darth Sidious, to Darth Vader|[[Darth Vader (2017) 13|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 13]]}} Following the Clone Wars, it was said that a select few decorated pilots, those who demonstrated an unwavering loyalty to their new emperor, were awarded the red "allegiance helmet."''[[Star Wars: Squadrons]]'' Sidious remained relatively unchallenged as Emperor for two [[Standard decade|decades]]. At first, however, he needed to maintain the illusion that the Empire was a simple revised form of the Republic, keeping the [[Imperial Senate]] active and making it seem like his rule was not a total one. It was his plan to totally disband the Senate once the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|DS-1 Death Star Mobile Battle Station]] was complete,[[Darth Vader (2015) 1|''Darth Vader'' (2015) 1]] enabling him to rule through fear alone,{{Film|IV}} while in the [[time]] being he consolidated his reign over the galaxy; he eliminated rivals, directed the Imperial Military to conquer planets beyond the Republic's frontier, and cemented what power was not already in his hands.''[[Leia, Princess of Alderaan]]''{{Andor|Announcement}} According to Palpatine himself, much of the Emperor's time was spent governing the galaxy.{{Rebels|Family Reunion – and Farewell}} However, he also ruled from a distance:[[Hidden Empire 5|''Hidden Empire'' 5]] as he was a single man who ruled the entire galaxy, most galactic citizens did not see their emperor.''[[The Princess and the Scoundrel]]'' Indeed, while he wanted to rule the galaxy, Palpatine did not want to have to deal with the boring bureaucratic work of governance and offloaded much of those duties onto his followers.{{InsiderCite|218|Rewind of the Jedi}} To maintain his rule, Palpatine thus relied on his proxies while he himself disappeared from public view. In the comfort of that privacy, Palpatine pursued research into the dark side with the aim of unlocking the secrets of living forever. All the same, Palpatine knew he needed to have at least a degree of appearance in his Empire, at least until the Death Star was completed; once the battle station was established, Palpatine intended for it to take his place as a reminder of dark power while he and Vader retreated to unlocking the deepest secrets of the dark side. It was Palpatine's ultimate goal to unlock the secrets needed to [[Alter Reality|alter reality itself]].[[Tarkin (novel)|''Tarkin'']] [[File:Threatofskywalker.png|thumb|right|300px|The Emperor ruled the galaxy for a generation with Darth Vader as his right hand.]] While Palpatine indeed made promises and threats to those he needed to keep in line, he relied on Vader to serve as his direct hand. Vader became known as the "[[Emperor's Fist]]."[[Age of Rebellion - Darth Vader 1|''Age of Rebellion - Darth Vader'' 1]] Certain other agents of Palpatine, such as Governor [[Gar Saxon]] of the planet [[Mandalore]], were known by the title of [[Emperor's Hand]]s.{{Rebels|Legacy of Mandalore}} Even during the lifespan of the Imperial Senate, the Emperor would rely on his massive military and a rule through fear, including [[Imperial Starfighter Pilot]]s. Notably, Palpatine relied greatly on such pilots during the [[Mid Rim uprisings]] when local [[Monarchy|monarchs]] refused to bow to his rule. Some [[HoloNet]] conspiracy theorists claimed that Palpatine had an heir to take over the Empire in the event of his death, but that was not true. In fact, the [[Emperor's adviser]] [[Sim Aloo]] hoped that either himself or his daughter [[Alinka Aloo|Alinka]] would take control of the Empire after Palpatine's death.{{StoryCite|story=Kernels and Husks|book=From a Certain Point of View: Return of the Jedi}} In total truth, however, Palpatine intended to live and rule forever. ====Flames of rebellion==== {{Quote|As Emperor, I reigned over the galaxy with unquestioned authority while Lord Vader administered my unrelenting justice. Any rebels musguided enough to stand in opposition to my rule were shown no mercy.|Darth Sidious|''[[Star Wars: The Secrets of the Sith]]''}} However, as a result of Sidious' efforts to subjugate the galaxy, the scattered cells of a growing rebellion gradually coalesced into the Rebel Alliance—a resistance movement determined to overthrow the Emperor and restore democracy. Throughout most of the [[Galactic Civil War]], Sidious directed his attention to destroying the rebellion that opposed his rule as Galactic Emperor. Some Imperial pilots came to see themselves as crusaders who fought in Palpatine's name, making it a dedicated mission to put out the flames of rebellion. Indeed, overall protocol amongst the military held that Palpatine's will kept the galaxy itself stable. [[File:ThrawnTreasonCoverArt.png|thumb|left|250px|Grand Admiral Mitth'raw'nuruodo "Thrawn" found himself set to become a new puppet for Palpatine, who hoped to extend his reach as Emperor to Thrawn's home, the Chiss Ascendancy.]] When [[Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo]] "Thrawn" argued the forces of the [[Grysk Hegemony]] were a threat to both his own people, the [[Chiss Ascendancy]], and the Empire, Sidious secretly decided the best option would be to forge an alliance between his regime and the Chiss by taking over the Ascendancy, becoming emperor of both the Chiss government and the Imperial state. Before Sidious could force Thrawn to betray his own people,''[[Thrawn: Treason]]'' the Grand Admiral was lost to Palpatine[[Star Wars (2020) 8|''Star Wars'' (2020) 8]] when the aspiring Jedi [[Ezra Bridger]] used a pod of [[Purrgil]] to take himself, Thrawn, and the [[Star Destroyer]] ''[[Chimaera]]'' off into hyperspace to [[Liberation of Lothal|save]] his homeworld of [[Lothal]]. With the dissolution of the Imperial Senate in [[1 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas: Updated Edition]]'' [[Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin]] and the regional governors were free to exercise full authority over their territories on the Emperor's behalf. His rule was also opposed by the [[Crimson Dawn]] syndicate, which he feared would unleash an [[Unidentified Sith Lord (Fermata Cage)|ancient Sith Lord]] from the [[Fermata Cage]]. Palpatine took a direct hand against the Dawn by joining Vader in the [[Battle at Amaxine Station]], where he was happy to exert his abilities and directly strike down enemies. The Crimson Dawn crisis would be followed by the [[Scourge crisis|scourge of the droids]],[[Dark Droids 1|''Dark Droids'' 1]] after which Palpatine faced yet another threat to his rule in the [[Schism Imperial]].{{PenguinComics|url=book/?isbn=75960609601504211|text=STAR WARS: DARTH VADER 42}} His effort to destroy the Rebel Alliance culminated in a plot to lure the [[Alliance Military|Alliance forces]] into a trap at [[Endor]]. The plan ultimately backfired however, resulting in the Emperor's [[death]] and the Empire's defeat at the [[Battle of Endor]] in [[4 ABY]]. ====Death of the Emperor==== {{Quote|In one battle, we lost our Emperor and gained a hundred warring factions.|[[Rella Sol]]|}} [[File:SentinelsManufactured-ShatteredEmpire4.png|thumb|right|250px|Sentinels were deployed with instructions to initiate Operation: Cinder in the aftermath of the Emperor's death.]] In the aftermath of the Battle of Endor, the remnants of the [[Imperial Navy]] regrouped to determine the next Emperor.''[[Lost Stars]]'' However, no clear chain of succession was evident, since Sidious had no known family and was always supposed to remain in power.''[[Aftermath: Life Debt]]'' The Empire broke into a number of warring factions over the future of the regime without Palpatine's continued rule. [[Grand General]] [[Levinous]] and [[Admiral]] [[Rolas]] both attempted to declare themselves the new emperor, but both were quickly deposed by their own forces for treason.''[[Star Wars: The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire]]'' Palpatine had laid out plans to punish and refine the Empire with his [[Contingency]] in the events of his death,''[[Aftermath: Empire's End]]'' beginning with the deployment of [[Sentinel (Contingency)|Sentinel droids]] that ordered the beginning of [[Operation: Cinder]].''[[Star Wars Battlefront II]]'' [[Governor]] [[Ubrik Adelhard]] hoped to maintain control of the [[Anoat sector]] with the [[Iron Blockade]] and the claim Palpatine was still alive. Grand Moff [[Lozen Tolruck]] and the ''[[Endor is A Lie]]'' poster claimed the same.''[[Star Wars Propaganda: A History of Persuasive Art in the Galaxy]]'' Although it was easy to prove Palpatine had died, the fact that most citizens never saw their Emperor made the lie reasonable. Other remnants claimed Palpatine was ruling from beyond the grave, which was somewhat true thanks to the plans he laid out in the Contingency. Rebel [[General]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] pondered who had given [[Commander]] [[Alecia Beck]] orders after the Battle of Endor and ultimately came to the conclusion there was a new major figure in the Empire who gave her the order to retreat. In Organa's mind, it was either a puppet master using the rumor of Palpatine's survival to rule or someone with the authority of the Emperor, possibly an heir named by Palpatine. [[File:SithEternal-DB.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Although the Empire ultimately fell, the Emperor was revered by various Sith cults in the galaxy.]] The Emperor inspired [[Sith cultist]]s across the galaxy,[[Aftermath (novel)|''Aftermath'']] notwithstanding his legacy as a reviled tyrant whose death was celebrated from the [[Core Worlds]] to the [[Outer Rim Territories]]. While the [[Sith Eternal]] operated mainly from [[Exegol]], a legendary Sith world in the [[Unknown Regions]]''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary]]'' another Sith [[Religion|cult]], the [[Acolytes of the Beyond]], remained in the known galaxy. Under the leadership of [[Yupe Tashu]], one of the [[Emperor's adviser]]s, the Acolytes scoured the galaxy seeking to collect [[Sith artifact]]s. One of their members was [[Ochi]], a trained [[Jedi killer]] who served the Emperor as his personal [[assassin]]. ===Mas Amedda=== {{Quote|I am the head of the Galactic Empire. I am its pinnacle!|Mas Amedda|}} [[File:EmperorsThroneRoom-2020DarthVader1.png|thumb|right|250px|Grand Vizier Mas Amedda became a powerless figurehead, after years of exercising authority in the Emperor's name.]] As head of the [[Imperial Ruling Council]] and the [[Imperial Senate]], Grand [[Vizier]] [[Mas Amedda]] effectively became the proxy Emperor in 4 ABY.''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of ''[[Aftermath: Life Debt]]'' to [[5 ABY]]. Amedda had served the Emperor for years; he was a politician in the Old Republic, serving as [[Vice Chair]] to [[Finis Valorum]] and Sheev Palpatine, in turn, before the Empire rose to power. Amedda was one of the few beings in the galaxy who knew that Palpatine was a Sith [[Lord]]. The self-proclaimed Emperor rewarded Amedda for his loyalty, allowing the [[Chagrian]] to remain at his side as Grand [[Vizier]] in the [[New Order]].{{Databank|mas-amedda|Mas Amedda}} While Amedda held power during the Emperor's reign, he did not succeed in consolidating his role as the Emperor's successor. As such, his power was largely limited to [[Coruscant]], where entire sectors of [[Imperial City]] rebelled against his reign, causing Amedda to become entrenched and trapped in government districts. Seeing Amedda's failure to take power, Grand Moff [[Plorest]] of [[Corusca sector|Coruscant's star sector]] attempted to declare himself the new emperor under the fictional [[Imperial Security Code 88173.1]]. The Imperial Military, however, completely ignored Plorest's "reign," which ended three days later in any case when he was killed by [[Plorest's lover|one of his lovers]]. Meanwhile, Amedda's request for assistance was refused by the [[Fleet Admiral]] [[Gallius Rax]], who did not allow [[Grand Admiral]] [[Rae Sloane]] to send reinforcements to the "proxy Emperor" Amedda as the [[throneworld]] had no place in his vision of a renewed Empire and had effectively took Amedda's powers and influence from him in [[5 ABY]]. [[File:ImperialCenter-ROTJ.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Amedda retreated to the Imperial Palace as the citizens of Coruscant openly rebelled against Imperial authority.]] In an act of despair and desperation, Amedda attempted to surrender himself into the custody of the [[New Republic]] during a secret meeting on [[Velusia]], believing there was no greater target or prize than himself. However, his offer was declined by [[Chancellor (New Republic)|Chancellor]] [[Mon Mothma]] and [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]], both of whom regarded Amedda not as an Emperor but rather an administrator. As such, they demanded that he find a way to regain his power in order to sign the the Galactic Empire's full surrender. With his reign effectively over upon returning to Coruscant, Amedda considered [[Death|suicide]] by jumping off of one of the [[Imperial Palace]]'s balconies. Instead, he and Sloane forged an alliance to undermine Rax and his cult-like ideas for the Empire by conducting an investigation into his past and preserving the [[New Order]]. By assisting the Grand [[Admiral]], Amedda hoped to secure his place under Sloane's Empire. ===Gallius Rax=== {{Quote|I only serve Palpatine.''"
"''Emperor Rax serves Palpatine, too.|Yupe Tashu and Windom Traducier|}} [[File:GalliusRexVariantClear-RUS-4.png|thumb|right|250px|Counselor Gallius Rax seized power and presided over the Empire's demise at the Battle of Jakku.]] In contrast to Amedda, who had lost [[Coruscant civil war|control]] over most of Coruscant after his request for reinforcements was denied, Gallius Rax successfully plotted his own rise to power following Palpatine's demise. However, he also continued to serve the late Emperor according to the Imperial [[agent]] [[Windom Traducier]]. Instead of openly ruling the galaxy, Rax sought to govern the Empire as the head of a new ruling body, the [[Shadow Council]], while supporting a figurehead as Palpatine's official successor. Although Rax was Emperor in effect, according to Traducier who referred to him as "Emperor Rax," he rejected the title and—in keeping with his intention to rule the Empire as the power behind the throne—created the position of [[Counselor to the Empire]] for himself. Officially, he continued to recognize Amedda as the leader of the Empire, but in reality Rax had the Chagrian [[Prisoner|imprisoned]] within the Imperial Palace. In secret, Rax planned to [[Contingency|eliminate]] the Shadow Council on [[Jakku]] with the exception of [[Commandant]] [[Brendol Hux]], who was essential to his plans. Rax ultimately perished in the [[Battle of Jakku]], however; and through the signing of the [[Galactic Concordance]], the Galactic Civil War ended with the remnants of the Empire capitulating to the New Republic. ===Rise of the Supreme Leader=== {{Quote|Kill the girl! End the Jedi, and become what your grandfather, Vader, could not. You will rule all the galaxy as the new Emperor.|Darth Sidious, to Kylo Ren|{{Film|IX}}}} [[File:Snoke_chillin_like_a_villain.png|thumb|left|250px|Supreme Leader Snoke was a genetic strandcast who ruled the First Order as Darth Sidious' proxy in power.]] Following the collapse of the Galactic Empire, a movement of [[Imperial officer]]s, [[noble]]s, and [[Scientist|technologists]] evolved into the [[First Order]].{{Databank|the-first-order|The First Order}} A successor of the Empire in all but name,''[[Star Wars Battlefront II]]'' the First Order was formed in the [[Unknown Regions]] and originally consisted of Imperial personnel, including Grand Admiral Rae Sloane, [[General]] Brendol Hux,''[[Star Wars: The Last Jedi: Expanded Edition]]'' and General [[Enric Pryde]]. Despite Sloane's ambitions to rule a new Empire, she and other Imperial leaders were ultimately supplanted by [[Supreme Leader]] [[Snoke]], an enigmatic [[humanoid]] [[alien]] who was strong with the [[dark side of the Force]].{{Databank|supreme-leader-snoke|Supreme Leader Snoke}} Unbeknownst to his own followers, Snoke was a [[Strand-Cast|strandcast]]—a [[Bioengineering|bioengineered]] construct—from Exegol. His creator was Darth Sidious; reborn in a [[Cloning|cloned]] body, the fallen Emperor made Snoke''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: Expanded Edition]]'' as his heir to the Contingency that ensured the Empire's destruction and rebirth as the First Order. In addition to his role as Sidious' proxy in power, Snoke was made to be the final test in the ascendancy of [[Ben Solo|Kylo Ren]]. As the grandson of [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]], Ren was the heir to the powerful bloodline of the [[Skywalker family]]. The Sith Eternal cultists designed Snoke to groom Ren into a worthy successor to the Sith legacy. By creating Snoke to ultimately die by Ren's hand, Sidious circumvented the Sith tradition in which an apprentice completed his training by killing the master. [[File:I_gave_everything_I_have_to_you.png|thumb|right|250px|Snoke was also designed to mold Kylo Ren, grandson of Darth Vader, into a worthy heir of the Sith.]] Snoke possessed unlimited power through his self-appointed position as Supreme Leader; despite this, he made no effort to claim the old title of Emperor. He also had little interest in mundane matters, preferring to focus on spiritual matters instead of the affairs of state. He therefore delegated authority to his high-ranking subordinates, and allowed the members of [[First Order High Command|High Command]] to control the [[First Order military]] in his name. Under his rule, a new generation of young, zealous leaders rose to power in the First Order, including [[Captain]] [[Phasma]], General [[Armitage Hux]] and Kylo Ren. They controlled the First Order's new [[superweapon]], [[Starkiller Base]], as an unofficial triumvirate.''[[Star Wars: The Force Awakens: The Visual Dictionary]]'' The New Republic sought to maintain peaceful relations with the Imperial remnants{{Databank|the-new-republic|The New Republic}} after reducing the Empire to a [[Inner systems' Imperial remnant|rump state]], hemmed in by war reparations and disarmament treaties. Nevertheless, the New Republic's final years were consumed by the [[Cold War]] as a result of the First Order's rise to power. When the New Republic fell in the [[Hosnian Cataclysm]] of [[34 ABY]], the armed forces of the First Order deployed across the galaxy, no longer restrained by their facade as a territorial defense force. As the First Order moved to seize control of the major [[star system]]s, Supreme Leader Snoke personally oversaw the military's efforts to destroy the [[Resistance]] that continued to oppose him in spite of the New Republic's destruction. His [[flagship]], the [[Mega-class Star Dreadnought|''Mega''-class Star Dreadnought]] ''[[Supremacy]]'', was at the head of a [[fleet]] of [[Resurgent-class Star Destroyer|''Resurgent''-class Star Destroyers]] that [[Battle of Oetchi|pursued]] the [[Resistance navy|Resistance fleet]] in the wake of the [[Battle of Starkiller Base]] and the [[Battle of D'Qar]]. [[File:Long_Live_The_Supreme_Leader.png|thumb|left|250px|Ren seized power as the new Supreme Leader by assassinating Snoke, an act that met with Sidious' approval.]] It was during this time that Kylo Ren assassinated his master and became the new Supreme Leader. With Snoke's death, Ren was free to exert his dominance over the First Order leadership, using his dark side powers to [[torture]] Hux into recognizing his claim. Ren's immediate goal was to end the [[First Order-Resistance War]], thereby allowing him to pursue his ambition of ruling the galaxy as the head of a new order. Despite remnants of the Resistance escaping from the [[First Order Army]] in the [[Battle of Crait]], the First Order nonetheless conquered large swathes of territory under Supreme Leader Ren. Ren consolidated his reign by suppressing dissent within the First Order and without. He also established the [[First Order Supreme Council|Supreme Council]], an advisory board of the highest-ranking [[First Order officer]]s to promote cooperation in their ranks{{Databank|first-order-supreme-council|First Order Supreme Council}} while keeping them divided through rivalry so as to prevent them from uniting against him.''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: Expanded Edition]]'' Although Hux survived the accession of Ren, their rivalry ultimately cost the general much of his authority and influence. Hux had little power or independence under Ren's leadership; moreover, Ren favored Enric Pryde whom he promoted to the rank of [[Allegiant General]]. During the last days of the war, Ren used his closest followers, the [[Knights of Ren]], as personal [[bodyguard]]s. ===Return of the Emperor=== {{Quote|And now, the power of two restores the one true Emperor.|Darth Sidious, to Ben Solo and Rey|}} [[File:InsiderIntel-Palpatine.png|thumb|right|300px|The Emperor survived his first death through the use of cloning and the dark side of the Force.]] The First Order relentlessly hunted the Resistance across the galaxy, using every resource at its disposal by order of Supreme Leader Kylo Ren.[[Allegiance 1|''Allegiance'' 1]] While Ren was determined to destroy his mother's movement for opposing him,{{Resistance|The Escape (episode)}} his personal agenda was to secure his power as ruler of the First Order. Therefore, he appointed the task of overseeing the war to his subordinates, not wishing to be distracted by the few remaining remnants of the Resistance. Having overthrown his master, Ren's ultimate goal was to consolidate the galaxy under his rule as the new Galactic Emperor, unlike his grandfather Anakin Skywalker who aspired towards the power of [[immortality]].''[[Skywalker: A Family at War]]'' During the war, however, the Supreme Leader discovered that Darth Sidious had returned from the grave, plotting from the shadows on the hidden Sith world of [[Exegol]]. Ren also learned that Sidious was responsible for the creation of Snoke, whose entire existence was based around the sole purpose of corrupting the young Ben Solo. By killing his master and usurping control of the First Order, Ren had taken a critical step on his path to complete submission to the dark side. He was ultimately Sidious' heir to a new [[Sith Empire]] which would conquer the galaxy with a mighty armada—the [[Final Order]]—of [[Xyston-class Star Destroyer|''Xyston''-class Star Destroyers]] and an [[Sith Eternal army|army]] of [[Sith trooper]]s. Aware of Ren's desire to rule over a new, galaxy-wide Sith Empire, Sidious offered him the title of Emperor on the condition that he killed [[Rey Skywalker|Rey]], the last Jedi who was also the former Emperor's [[Palpatine family|granddaughter]]. Ren ultimately accepted this mandate, and intended to not only succeed where his grandfather failed by ruling all the galaxy as the new Emperor but to also finish what he started by destroying the Sith and the Jedi.''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: A Junior Novel]]'' [[File:ReyMeetsPalpatine-TROS.jpg|thumb|left|250px|After Ren's redemption, Sidious tried to seduce his granddaughter Rey to the dark side in order to make her Empress.]] Ren's eventual [[Mission to Kef Bir|return]] to the [[Light side of the Force|light]] undermined Sidious' plans for him. Having secured control of the First Order through Allegiant General Enric Pryde, Sidious turned his attention to preparing Rey as his sole successor. During the [[Battle of Exegol]], Sidious encouraged her to take his throne as "Empress Palpatine" with the plan to take control over her body once she gave into darkness.{{SW|url=news/star-wars-inside-intel-palpatines-contingency-plan|text=''Star Wars'' Inside Intel: Palpatine's Contingency Plan|int=Star Wars Inside Intel}} His efforts to turn Rey to the dark side of the Force failed, however, due to the intervention of the former Kylo Ren, who reclaimed his identity as Ben Solo. With both of his would-be heirs standing against them, Sidious attacked them through the dark side, but in doing so he discovered that they were a [[Force dyad|dyad in the Force]]. [[Force drain|Draining]] the life force of their [[Force-bond]] to heal himself, Sidious announced his return as the one true Emperor. [[File:The_death_of_Sidious.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Emperor's cloned body was destroyed during the Battle of Exegol.]] As Sidious prepared to unleash the [[Axial superlaser|planet-killer]] [[warship]]s of the Sith fleet upon the galaxy, Rey was able to rise up with the strength of all the Jedi backing her. Despite Sidious harnessing all the powers of the Sith in an effort to kill his granddaughter, Rey was able to vanquish the Emperor at the cost of her life, although she was later [[Force healing|revived]] by Solo. With the Emperor's second death and the destruction of the [[Sith Eternal military|Sith Eternal forces]], the Sith fleet was never launched from Exegol. As a result, multiple planets across the galaxy [[Uprising against the First Order|began revolting against]] the military rule of the First Order. ==Style of office== {{Quote|This is the Emperor's dream.''"
"''Can't we just call him Palpatine—in private, I mean?|Galen Walton Erso and Lyra Erso|''[[Catalyst: A Rogue One Novel]]''}} [[File:ImperialFigureheads.png|thumb|left|250px|The Galactic Emperor was addressed as "''Your Majesty''" and other such titles by those under him, while his Sith apprentice addressed him as his master.]] ''Majesty'' was an honorific style used by Darth Sidious during his reign as Galactic Emperor. In direct reference to the Emperor, it took on the form "Your Majesty." Other honorific styles applied to the Emperor were "Your Highness," "Your Eminence,"[[Darth Vader (2020) 12|''Darth Vader'' (2020) 12]] and "His Grace." In the context of nonofficial, everyday conversations, Sidious was generally referred to as just "the Emperor," even between Imperial [[officer]]s. At the beginning of his reign, [[clone trooper]]s referred to him as "Sir" and "My Lord." [[Moff]] Wilhuff Tarkin once addressed the Emperor as "Your Excellency,"[[Darth Vader (2017) 5|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 5]] which was Palpatine's honorific style as Supreme Chancellor. Deputy Director [[Harus Ison]] of the [[Imperial Security Bureau]] greeted Sidious by addressing him as "My Lord Emperor" when speaking of the theft of the ''[[Carrion Spike]]''. Certain individuals had their own ways to address the Emperor. [[Lyra Erso]] still referred to the Emperor by his surname, Palpatine, in contrast to her [[Marriage|husband]], [[Doctor]] [[Galen Walton Erso]], who used Sidious' title when speaking of him. As the [[Sith apprentice]] of Darth Sidious, Darth Vader addressed his [[Sith Master]] as "my master" or "master," a sign of their master–disciple relation in the dark arts of the Force. Vader would also use the possessive determiner "thy" instead of the more common "your," when inquiring his Master's will.{{Film|V}} Following the Emperor's demise, his political right-hand, Grand Vizier Mas Amedda, was addressed as "Glorious leader of the Empire" by Counselor Gallius Rax. By then Amedda ruled in appearance only, Rax having assumed control of the Empire as its ''de facto'' leader. The title of Empress was the [[Gender|female]] equivalent to Emperor. Sidious once referred to his granddaughter Rey as "Empress Palpatine" while attempting to mold her as his successor. ==Residence== ===Imperial Executive Building=== {{Main|Imperial Executive Building}} {{Quote|Setting up the mercenary contract from the Emperor's office didn't work either? No mistrust? No dramatic accusations?|[[Barokki]], speaking with his [[Unidentified Imperial officer (Coruscant)|accomplice]]|[[Darth Vader (2017) 12|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 12]]}} [[File:EmperorsOffice2-2017DarthVader5.png|thumb|right|250px|The Emperor still utilized his old office as chancellor during the early days of his reign.]] The [[Emperor's office]], located in the Imperial Executive Building on Coruscant, served as the Emperor's seat of power in the early days of his reign. The office suite served as his headquarters since his time as Supreme Chancellor. Although the Emperor still used it as an audience chamber, the office no longer had his desk and chairs save for the chair he used during his chancellery. The [[Emperor's Royal Guard]] was stationed in the office for the Emperor's security, just as they had been during Palpatine's chancellery. ===Imperial Palace=== {{Main|Imperial Palace}} {{Quote|The Jedi Temple on Coruscant''…'' It doesn't exist anymore. It's the Imperial Palace now.|[[Kreel]], to [[Luke Skywalker]]|[[Star Wars (2015) 10|''Star Wars'' (2015) 10]]}} [[File:Imperial_Temple.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The Imperial Palace, once known as the Jedi Temple, was the Emperor's seat of power on Coruscant.]] Darth Sidious continued to rule the galaxy from Coruscant, now known as Imperial Center, after the Clone Wars. As Emperor, he established the Imperial Palace as his headquarters on the galactic capital. Prior to the Age of the Empire, the palace served as the Jedi Order's center of operations, known as the Jedi Temple.{{Databank|jedi-temple|Jedi Temple}} With the fall of the Jedi, however, the Emperor had the temple extensively renovated and repurposed to serve as his personal residence. Though Coruscant remained the Empire's official capital, with the proxy Emperor Amedda remaining on the throneworld as a virtual prisoner in the Imperial Palace, Counselor Rax preferred ruling as Emperor in effect from his [[flagship]], the [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought|''Executor''-class Star Dreadnought]] ''[[Ravager]]''. During his reign, the warship contained a private upper garden for recreational purposes. It was thought to be the last surviving [[Super Star Destroyer]] in the Imperial Navy by the time of the [[Rebellion on Akiva]], and was destroyed on Jakku during the final battle of the Galactic Civil War. ===Sith Citadel=== {{Main|Sith Citadel}} {{Quote|Find the Wayfinder, get to Exegol… And bring an end to the conflict once and for all.|Rey, quoting Luke Skywalker's writings|}} [[File:Throne_of_the_Sith.png|thumb|right|250px|Located in the Sith Citadel, the Dark Throne was offered to Ren and Rey before Sidious claimed it as the one true Emperor.]] The Sith Citadel was located on Exegol, one of the oldest Sith bastions dating back a thousand years before the fall of the Galactic Republic and the rise of the Empire—when the ancient Sith ruled the galaxy. A massive, forbidding citadel was also ancient in origin, filled with old, crumbling statuary. Serving as the base of the Sith Eternal cult, the citadel held many sinister secrets. Despite the Emperor's demise, his body was preserved and sustained deep within the citadel, which also housed several duplicates of the entity known as Snoke. The citadel contained a [[Amphitheater of the Sith Eternal|throne room]] housing the [[Throne of the Sith]]. Opposite of the throne was an amphitheater capable of holding the many cultists who kept belief in the Sith religion alive. It was the site of both Sidious' restoration to power and his subsequent destruction. As neither Ben Solo nor Rey accepted the Dark Throne, Sidious claimed it for himself along with his old title of Emperor. With his destruction, however, much of the citadel was destroyed along with the throne room and the amphitheater. ==Protection== ===Emperor's Royal Guard=== {{Main|Emperor's Royal Guard}} {{Quote|The Emperor's personal protectors—handpicked from the very best of his forces. Out of ''millions'' of soldiers, they are unsurpassed.|[[Korin Pers]], on the Royal Guard|[[Lando 3|''Lando'' 3]]}} [[File:Emperor_Sidious_Guards_SWTDS.png|thumb|left|220px|The Emperor's Royal Guard comprised the best soldiers in the Empire.]] The Emperor's Royal Guard was an order of elite bodyguards charged with the duty of protecting the Galactic Emperor.{{Databank|imperial-royal-guard|Imperial Royal Guard}} Chosen from the very best of the Imperial Military, their loyalty and obedience to Emperor Palpatine was without question. Additionally, the Emperor was guarded by [[Imperial shock trooper|clone shock troopers]] of the [[Coruscant Guard]] before the [[cloning]] production on [[Kamino]] was shut down,[[Darth Vader (2017) 2|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 2]] after which the Emperor's security was provided mainly by Royal Guards and Imperial [[stormtrooper]]s.{{Databank|senate-guard|Senate Guard}} Royal Guards wielded [[force pike]]s, a [[staff]]-like [[Melee weapon|weapon]]{{Databank|force-pike|Force Pike}} that had a [[Vibro-weapon|vibro-edged head]]. Their uniforms consisted of [[Color|crimson]] [[robe]]s and [[armor]], which included featureless scarlet [[Helmet|masks]] that concealed the sentinels' identities. The remnants of the Royal Guard continued to serve the Empire despite the Emperor's death, with several guardsmen rallying to Palpatine's potential successors such as Grand [[Admiral]] Rae Sloane and Fleet Admiral Gallius Rax. During the final months of the Galactic Civil War, Sloane's Royal Guards [[Attack on Chandrila|attacked]] and killed several [[Senate Guard (New Republic)|New Republic Senate Guards]] at the [[Imperial–Republic peace talks|peace summit]] on [[Chandrila]]. At the Battle of Jakku, a [[Arliz Hadrassian's brother|Royal Guard]] served in the ranks of Rax's faction and was ultimately killed while fighting against the forces of the New Republic. ===Sovereign Protectors=== {{Main|Sovereign Protector}} {{Quote|The might of the Final Order will soon be ready.|Darth Sidious|}} [[File:Sovereign-Protector-CEUEE.png|thumb|right|200px|The best Sith troopers served as the Emperor's Sovereign Protectors.]] The Sovereign Protectors were the Emperor's elite bodyguards during the rise of the Sith Eternal. Drawn from the ranks of the elite [[Sith trooper]]s, only the best were elevated to the status of Sovereign Protector. In addition to their crimson armor, Sovereign Protectors wore a scarlet [[cape]] and were stationed throughout the Sith Citadel on Exegol. Like the Sith troopers in general, Sovereign Protectors were the culmination of generations of work in which the Empire sought to strip its soldiers of their individuality, replacing it with fervent loyalty to the Emperor's will. During the Clone Wars, Sidious was dismayed to discover that the genetically engineered clone troopers still exhibited disconcerting amounts of free will despite numerous alterations to their genetic structure. Though the Sovereign Protectors were not clones, they had to undergo flash-imprinting and loyalty conditioning that were built upon the [[Kaminoan]] procedures of earlier generations. As a result, Sovereign Protectors were even more loyal and machine-like than the stormtroopers who trained almost since birth under the First Order.
